title: Validation Curves knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the central idea of “Validation Curves”?
options: The method always performs better than a simple baseline, regardless of the task.
Validation estimates performance on data that did not guide the fitted choices. Keep the final test set separate from preprocessing, feature selection, and tuning decisions.
The method proves that every prediction will be correct on all future datasets.
The method removes the need to inspect data quality or define an evaluation strategy.
questions.answer_key: Validation estimates performance on data that did not guide the fitted choices. Keep the final test set separate from preprocessing, feature selection, and tuning decisions.
questions.explanation: The lesson frames the topic this way: Validation estimates performance on data that did not guide the fitted choices. Keep the final test set separate from preprocessing, feature selection, and tuning decisions. The other options make unsupported guarantees.

questions.prompt: What is a sound first step when applying “Validation Curves” to a new task?
options: Name the inputs, assumptions, and output for validation_curve(); then test it on representative data.
Tune against the final test set until the preferred metric increases.
Remove records that produce unexpected outcomes without investigating them.
Assume the default parameters are best for every dataset.
questions.answer_key: Name the inputs, assumptions, and output for validation_curve(); then test it on representative data.
questions.explanation: Define the input, output, assumptions, and evidence needed. For validation_curve(), a small representative check is more useful than blind tuning.

questions.prompt: What conclusion is appropriately cautious after trying “Validation Curves”?
options: A single successful run proves fairness, robustness, and production readiness.
A higher training score alone proves generalization to unseen data.
An internal estimator score replaces domain review and operational monitoring.
A successful small example is useful evidence about that example, but generalization, risks, and limitations still need separate checks.
questions.answer_key: A successful small example is useful evidence about that example, but generalization, risks, and limitations still need separate checks.
questions.explanation: A demonstration only supports conclusions within its scope. Evaluate representative unseen cases and report limitations before production use.
